title: What If Earth Had No Mountains or Trenches? No Land at All

scenes.text: What if Earth had no mountains and no ocean trenches? There would be no dry land at all.
Today the oceans cover about 70.8 percent of Earth and hold roughly 1.3 billion cubic kilometers of water.
Earth's whole surface is about 510 million square kilometers. Now spread that water evenly over all of it.
The result is a global ocean roughly 2.6 kilometers deep. That's over a mile and a half of water.
Nothing would stick out. From Everest's summit to the Challenger Deep is only about 20 kilometers.
That's just 0.16 percent of Earth's width. Mountains aren't towering giants. They're tiny wrinkles on a nearly smooth planet.

description:
What if Earth were perfectly smooth, with no mountains and no trenches?
The oceans would cover everything, about 2.6 kilometers deep, because our biggest mountains are tiny wrinkles on a huge planet.
What should we run through next?
